listAcquisitions.sDispositionRationale: The remote client's OpenSSH launch, on the researcher's own host lane, outside the carrier's scope by design (design section 8). It mutates nothing on this machine: it starts ssh, which opens a forward and runs a FIXED remote command. The argv is built by fsaBuildSshCommand from source text plus two validated values -- an int()-cast port and a destination that fnValidateSshDestination has matched against ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(@[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?$ and refused if it begins with a dash. The destination is its own argv element and never enters the remote command string, which matters because OpenSSH hands that string to the far side's LOGIN SHELL; this is also why the command carries no project name, a value that may legally contain a space. No shell=True, no user-supplied text in the command. Review relied on: fnValidateSshDestination, fiChooseLocalPort (port bounded 1..65535), fsaBuildSshCommand (the only argv builder), and tests/testRemoteClient.py, which pins the option-looking and shell-looking destinations as refusals and the absence of --project.

The remote helper's detached hub launch, on the researcher's own host lane, outside the carrier's scope by design (design section 8: the hub itself is a trust judgement, not a capability the carrier grants). The argv is FIXED SOURCE TEXT in _fprocessStartDetachedHub -- sys.executable, -m vaibify, --no-browser, --port -- with the only interpolation an int()-cast port already bounded to 1..65535 by fnRemoteHelperCommand. No shell, no user string, and nothing from the SSH client reaches the argv: the client sends only a port, and fdictParseStartupRecord refuses a record naming any other one. The child is deliberately detached (start_new_session) because a closing laptop must not stop a running pipeline; it is therefore NOT journaled as a gated operation, because the journal keys by project and settles only on a dead holder with an empty process group, so a long-lived hub would leave a record that never settles and would permanently veto both the ownership reaper and idle shutdown. Review relied on: fnRemoteHelperCommand (port bound), _fnRefuseForeignListener and fdictFindCompatibleHub (a port already serving is refused, not adopted blindly), and the sessionRoutes _fprocessLaunchDetachedHub precedent this copies.

`vaibify sessions stop` on the researcher's own host lane, which is outside the carrier's scope by design (design section 8: a trust judgement about the hub itself needs no capability). The PID comes from vaibify's own session registry and is checked for recycle-proof liveness before the signal; the signal is SIGTERM to a hub this user started.

SIGTERM to the caffeinate helper THIS process launched and holds the pid of. Not a container mutation and reachable from no request lane: it runs on claim/release and at shutdown, so a carrier admission would have nothing to admit.

Signal 0, delivering nothing -- the journal's own emptiness probe for helper and host-exec records. Callers reach it only through the probe catalog, which has already checked the recorded pid and group are usable.

Signal 0, delivering nothing -- the shared PID-existence probe behind every lock, lease and journal staleness check. PermissionError counts as alive (the process exists under another user), which is the conservative direction: it never reaps a live holder.

The router's Docker-only tail delegation: __getattr__ forwards an attribute READ to the Docker leg verbatim, raising the typed DockerLegUnavailableError when no leg exists. It mints no authority: the delegated methods are DockerConnection's own, each carrying its own admission gates, and the resource-routed surface is twelve explicit methods above it, not this fallback.

The idle self-shutdown signals os.getpid() -- this process, and only this process. The busy veto that precedes it reads dictContainerOwners so a hub can never self-retire mid-run. There is no other target reachable from this call. Re-confirmed 2026-08-19 after the idle timeout became live-tunable: the signal target is still os.getpid() and the busy veto still precedes it, so the judgement is unchanged and only its anchor moved.

Signal 0 only — a liveness PROBE, never a delivery: resolves an undiscovered HOST terminal record fail-closed (a live unproven shell quarantines; a provably dead stub settles). The pid is the record's own journaled identity.

Signal 0 delivers nothing: this is an existence probe, not a signal. It answers whether a recorded group still has members, which is what makes host mode's weaker quiescence claim sayable. The same fbIsUsablePid guard applies, so a zero group id can never be probed as the caller's own.

The leader-group sweep beside the per-member delivery in fnSignalSessionMembers, for anything that joined the group between the enumeration and the signal. Usable-pid guarded (killpg(0) would signal the hub's own group), TERM/KILL allowlisted, quiet on refusal.

Per-member delivery for the terminal drain (fnSignalSessionMembers): signals ONLY pids the host leg's session-wide sweep enumerated, TERM/KILL allowlisted, quiet on refusal — the terminate-and-prove caller decides on the PROOF. Needed because killpg cannot reach a job the shell's job control moved to its own group; this module is the single host signal-judgement seam.

The one site that signals something vaibify did not create in this process: a host project's journaled process GROUP, on the researcher's own machine. Guarded three ways, each with a registered falsification -- the group is only ever one the host-exec journal recorded; it is signalled only while the holder pid is provably the recorded one (fbIsProcessAliveSince, recycle-proof), an unprovable identity being reported and routed to reconciliation rather than guessed at; and fbIsUsablePid refuses a zero or absent group id, which killpg would otherwise read as the CALLER's own group. Reached from POST /api/pipeline/{id}/kill under a mode-(b) carrier, and from `vaibify reconcile --terminate-recorded` on the host lane.

The host terminal's PTY pair. Opened only inside fdictLaunchTerminalShellSuspended — the gateway's own suspended-gate launch, which asserts command admission and spawns the shell blocked behind a dedicated gate pipe; the terminal seam (terminalSession.py, the only module that prepares terminal execution records) journals the pid with the terminal kind BEFORE the gate opens, and the drain machinery terminates-and-proves the recorded session. Supporting symbols: _S_TERMINAL_LAUNCH_STUB, fnPromoteHostTerminalOperation, fdictTerminateAndProveRecord.

The host gateway's single subprocess import. Every launch goes through _ftLaunchGatedAndStream: suspended spawn behind a stdin gate, host-exec journal record promoted and identity-gated (fnPromoteJournaledHostExec) before release, admission asserted (fnAssertContainerCommandAdmitted / fnAssertDurableExecAdmitted) at the two public entry points; testHostSubprocessConfinement pins this module as the only launcher under vaibify/host/.

listRows.sExclusionRationale: The containment authority's own signal leg, not a route-reachable mutation: it fires only inside terminalContainment.fdictTerminateAndProveRecord (session close, safe reaper, shutdown, reconcile), against a process group recorded in the terminal journal record it is settling. Supporting symbols: _fsBuildProcessGroupScript, ftRunRootShellProbe, _I_CONTAINER_DEFAULT_UID, terminalContainment._fdictSignalAndAwaitEmpty.

listRows.sExclusionRationale: This row IS the enforcement point, not a caller of it: admission is asserted at its two public entry points (fnAssertContainerCommandAdmitted / fnAssertDurableExecAdmitted) before it runs, and every launch is write-ahead journaled as host-exec with the child suspended behind a gate until its identity is persisted. A carrier admits callers; this is the gate they hit. Re-reviewed 2026-08-15 when the fingerprint moved: the launch gained an environment argument composed by _fdictComposeLaunchEnvironment (inherited os.environ plus an optional caller overlay -- adds or shadows entries, never replaces the environment), which changes what the child SEES, not what may launch one.
listRows.sLogicalOperation: the single gated launch every host-project subprocess goes through
listRows.sOperationMetadata: command text in via parameter (the declared opaque-subprocess-command blind-spot row); environment is inherited plus an optional overlay (determinism data); bounded lane kills its recorded group on timeout; durable lane relies on the journaled group identity for Cancel and quiescence

listRows.sExclusionRationale: The host terminal's launch primitive — a separate authority, the same shape as the Docker exec-id PTY cluster: its gates are the WebSocket ownership gate at the route and the terminal journal record the seam writes before the gate pipe opens, not a carrier. Command admission is still asserted, so an enforced lane reaching it without a carrier refuses. Supporting symbols: fnAssertContainerCommandAdmitted, _S_TERMINAL_LAUNCH_STUB, fnPromoteHostTerminalOperation, testOnlyTheGatedRouteConstructsATerminalSession.
listRows.sLogicalOperation: spawn the host terminal shell suspended behind its gate pipe
listRows.sOperationMetadata: fixed argv (the stub plus the gate fd); the shell is always /bin/bash -i on a fresh PTY in its own session; no caller-supplied command text exists on this path

listRows.sExclusionRationale: A typed read: the adapter hands a PATH and a declared operation name to the audited-read carve-out, never a command, so it reaches no mutation-capable primitive and there is nothing for a carrier to admit. It was `test -f`/`test -d` through the general exec primitive until 2026-08-04, which the gate had to treat as mutating -- so under an enforced lane an existence check was refused, and the level gate above it read the refusal as 'unverified' and downgraded the workflow's badge.
